facts.text: Weston, Missouri was founded in 1837 and was the farthest western settlement in the United States until Texas joined the Union in 1845.
The town’s name comes from First Sergeant Tom Weston, who laid out the original town plan after the land was purchased by a former Army dragoon.
Weston is home to the McCormick Distilling Company, the oldest continuously operated distillery west of the Mississippi River, founded in 1856.
The historic downtown district, founded in 1837, still hosts the only surviving historic hotel from Weston’s heyday.
Weston’s early commercial buildings show French and German influences, reflecting traders from New Orleans and immigrants from Canada.
The town served as a major jumping-off point for the Santa Fe, Oregon, and California Trails during the Gold Rush era.
